summary: No changes to existing covenants are warranted; a new inventory covenant is added to address weakened inventory assumption evidenced by increased days in inventory.

clauses.rationale: Current Minimum Core Assets Test already reflects Amazon break fee terms; no new evidence requires modification.
Financial statement delivery remains timely; no evidence of deterioration.
Monthly deliverables and compliance certification continue as required; no issues identified.
Amazon Break Fee sweep provisions align with confirmed termination fee payment and usage.
Notice of default clause remains adequate; no evidence of changed default risk.
Inventory days rose to 161-163, indicating misalignment with run rates and higher cash consumption, justifying a new inventory limit.
clauses.change: Add a maximum inventory covenant to limit inventory levels (e.g., inventory days or amount).

evidence.quote: GAAP days in inventory (DII) was 161 days, compared with 95 days at the end of 2022.

drift_reasons: Added a new inventory covenant to address weakened inventory assumption, which alters risk coverage and constitutes a substantive change.
